run.procedureSummary: Start: x0=(3,6,6,2,2,1), s=0, all flags INACTIVE. Each cycle runs these steps, each one finished across the whole vector before the next starts. 1) Load: add the cycle's row of b to x, with no bounds enforced. 2) Projection sweep, Gauss-Seidel order 1 to 6: if x_i>c_i, set x_i=c_i and add the excess to x_{i+1} before visiting it, so overflow cascades; component 6's excess goes to s. 3) Active-set update on the projected x: INACTIVE becomes ACTIVE when x_i>=u_i, ACTIVE becomes INACTIVE when x_i<=d_i, and otherwise the flag holds. Each flip is logged. 4) Jacobi shed: compute all six amounts from the same x first. An INACTIVE component sends floor(x_i/4) to s. An ACTIVE component sends floor(x_i/2) to x_{i-1}, and component 1 sends its share to s. Then apply all of them at once, with no projection afterwards. 5) Penalty: if sum(x) is strictly greater than 38, replace every x_i with floor(x_i/2), add the amount removed to s, and record the cycle.

openPoints.point: Order of the flag update and the shed
openPoints.assumption: Step 4 uses the flags set in step 3 of the same cycle, including flips made in that cycle.
The test uses sum(x) over the six components only, without s, measured after the shed. A total of exactly 38 does not trigger it (cycle 5 ends at 38, so no penalty fires).

openPoints.point: Cascade amounts in the projection sweep
openPoints.assumption: The overflow pushed from x_i is added before x_{i+1} is clipped. It can therefore make x_{i+1} go over its bound and cascade further.
lossTotal is the final slack s, which collects component-6 projection overflow, INACTIVE sheds, component 1's ACTIVE share and the penalty halvings.
After the shed, components are left above c_i as the write-up says (for example x2=10>8 at the end of cycle 5). They are not clipped at the end of the run.

run.preReadNotes: The write-up is self-contained and has no embedded instructions beyond the line rules. I applied its rules exactly as written.
